learning_experiences: kutambua silabi za sauti lengwa (p/b, t/d, k/g, ch/j) kutokana na maneno kwenye vitabu, ubaoni au kwa kutumia vifaa vya kidijitali,
kusikiliza silabi za sauti lengwa zikitamkwa na mwalimu, mgeni mwalikwa au kutoka kwa vifaa vya kidijitali kama vile kinasasauti na rununu,
kutamka silabi za sauti lengwa na vitanzandimi akiwa na wenzake,

kusikiliza vitanzandimi vilivyoundwa kutokana na maneno yenye sauti lengwa vikikaririwa na mwalimu, mgeni mwalikwa au katika vifaa vya kidijitali (kwa mfano. baba alivua papa katika bahari pana, kila Chacha akila hali chakula kikichacha),
kuunda vitanzandimi vyepesi vinavyotokana na vitate husika akiwa na wenzake,
kuunda vitanzandimi kwenye vifaa vya kidijitali na kushirikiana na wenzake mitamboni kuvirekebisha,
kushiriki majadiliano kuhusu sababu za kukariri vitanzandimi maishani mwake.
key_inquiry_questions: Matamshi bora yana umuhimu gani katika mawasiliano?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhiriki katika mijadala kuhusu matamshi bora.
Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anapotumia kifaa cha kidijitali kusikiliza sauti.
Hamu ya ujifunzaji: mwanafunzi anapoendelea kukariri vitanzandimi pia anapotoa muhtasari wa kifungu ili kupata kuelewa zaidi.
Ubunifu: mwanafunzi anaposhiriki katika kuunda vitanzandimi.
sub_strands.values:
Umoja: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika kujadili maana na matumizi ya msamiati lengwa.
Uwajibikaji: mwanafunzi anapotumia kifaa cha kidijitali kuunda vitanzandimi pamoja na wenzake.
Uzalendo: mwanafunzu anapotangamana na wenzake kutoka jamii mbalimbali katika kutamka silabi za sauti lengwa na vitanzandimi.
sub_strands.pcis: Utangamano wa kijamii: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake kutoa maneno tofautitofauti kuunda vitanzandimi kwenye kifaa cha kidijitali na kuvirekebisha.
sub_strands.links: Mwanafunzi anaweza kuhusisha stadi ya matamshi bora katika somo hili na ujifunzaji wa dhana hiyo katika somo la English.

kutamka silabi zinazotokana na sauti p/b, t/d, k/g, ch/j
kutamka vitanzandimi vinavyoundwa kwa silabi za sauti p/b, t/d, k/g, ch/j
kuunda vitanzandimi kutokana na sauti p/b, t/d, k/g, ch/j
kuchangamkia kukariri vitanzandimi vinavyoundwa kwa silabi za sauti zinazokaribiana kimatamshi katika kuboresha matamshi yake

skills.name: Tofautisha sauti p/b, t/d, k/g na ch/j katika silabi, maneno na vitanzandimi
skills.mastery: Hears, says and writes the right sound in syllables and words with p/b, t/d, k/g na ch/j (tamu and damu, koti and goti), picks the word that matches the meaning, and tells a real kitanzandimi from an ordinary sentence, in 8 of 10 new items.

prerequisites.reason: Hearing the syllables of a target sound in Grade 3 is the base for telling two close sounds apart.
Every Kiswahili syllable ends in one of the five vowels; the child must know them to split words.

misconceptions.error: Hears or says /d/ for /t/, so tamu (sweet) becomes damu (blood).

example.question: Mwalimu anasema: "tamu". Umesikia neno lipi?

misconceptions.cause: p/b, t/d, k/g and ch/j are made at the same place in the mouth and differ only in voice; Kalenjin languages, for example, do not separate them, so the child hears one sound and writes either letter.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Mwalimu anasema: "tamu". Umesikia neno lipi?" with "damu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Say the pair slowly with a hand on the throat (or watching the lips); the child says which word was heard before writing.
misconceptions.feedback: Sikiliza tena: "tamu" ina sauti /t/. "damu" ni neno lingine lenye maana nyingine.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Writes the word with the letter of the other sound (goti where koti is meant).

example.question: Jaza pengo: ___ maana yake ni "a coat".

misconceptions.cause: The child spells as he speaks; if the two sounds are one sound in his speech, the letter is a guess.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Jaza pengo: ___ maana yake ni "a coat"." with "goti" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Pair each spelling with its meaning on a card; the child sorts the cards by meaning, then by letter.
misconceptions.feedback: Neno lenye maana ya "a coat" ni "koti". "goti" lina maana ya "a knee".
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks the two words are one word said in two ways, with one meaning.

example.question: "koti" na "goti" ni maneno yenye maana moja?

misconceptions.cause: The child has heard both said by different people for the same thing and takes the difference for an accent.
misconceptions.reveals: The question ""koti" na "goti" ni maneno yenye maana moja?" with "ndiyo" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Use both words in two sentences that cannot swap: the child says which sentence breaks.
misconceptions.feedback: Hapana. "koti" ni a coat, na "goti" ni a knee.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Takes any long sentence for a kitanzandimi, though it does not repeat the target sounds.

example.question: Ni kipi ni kitanzandimi?
example.correct_answer: Baba na bibi wanapika pilau na pombe ya bibi bila pilipili.

misconceptions.cause: The child thinks a kitanzandimi is any sentence that is hard to say, not one built by repeating close sounds.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni kipi ni kitanzandimi?" with "Mama amerudi nyumbani jioni." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Underline the target sounds in the real kitanzandimi; count them; the ordinary sentence has few or none.
misconceptions.feedback: Kitanzandimi hurudia sauti zinazokaribiana, kama p/b, t/d, k/g na ch/j, ili kiwe kigumu kutamka.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Breaks the word into syllables at the wrong place, so the target sound is lost (ta-mu read as two wrong parts).

example.question: Neno "tamu" lina silabi zipi?

misconceptions.cause: In Kiswahili every syllable ends in a vowel, and a nasal with its consonant (nd, mb, nj, ng) starts one syllable; the child splits by letters, not by sound.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno "tamu" lina silabi zipi?" with "t-amu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Clap the word: one clap per vowel; the nasal goes with the consonant after it.
misconceptions.feedback: Kila silabi ya Kiswahili huishia kwa irabu: ta-mu.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

learning_experiences: kutambua msamiati wa nyumbani (k.v. meza, sebule, balbu/globu, kizingiti, fremu, neti, tendegu, mtoto wa meza, mvungu, figa, kinu, tumbuu, kochi, kupiga deki) uliotumiwa katika kifungu cha hadithi,
kushirikiana na wenzake kujadili maana na matumizi ya msamiati lengwa katika sentensi,
kuimba nyimbo zinazolenga msamiati lengwa,
kusoma kifungu kinachohusiana na suala lengwa kwenye kitabu au kwenye tarakilishi akiwa na wenzake,
kujibu maswali kutokana na kifungu alichosoma,
kutoa muhtasari wa ujumbe wa kifungu alichokisoma,
kumweleza mzazi au mlezi wake ujumbe wa kifungu alichokisoma.
key_inquiry_questions: Unazingatia nini ili kupata ujumbe katika kifungu cha hadithi?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhiriki katika mijadala na kazi za vikundi.
Kujiamini: mwanafunzi anapotoa muhtasari wa kifungu na kujibu maswali ipasavyo.
sub_strands.values:
Heshima: mwanafunzi anapothamini maoni ya wenzake wanapojadili maana na matumizi ya msamiati lengwa katika sentensi.
Upendo: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika kikundi na kusaidiana.
sub_strands.pcis: Usalama mtandaoni: mwanafunzi anapotumia tarakilishi au projekta kuchora vifaa vya nyumbani kwa uangalifu.
sub_strands.links: Mwanafunzi anaweza kuhusisha stadi ya kusoma kwa ufahamu katika somo hili na ujifunzaji wa dhana hiyo katika somo la English.

outcomes.text: kutambua msamiati wa suala lengwa uliotumika katika kifungu cha hadithi ili kuimarisha ufahamu
kutumia msamiati lengwa kwa usahihi katika sentensi
kutoa muhtasari wa ujumbe wa kifungu cha hadithi
kujenga mazoea ya usomaji bora katika maisha ya kila siku

skills.name: Elewa na tumia msamiati wa kifungu
skills.mastery: Gives the meaning of a word from the sentence it is in and picks the word that fits a gap in a sentence, without choosing a look-alike, a nearby or an opposite word, in 8 of 10 new items.

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.
Most theme vocabulary is nouns of the home.

leads_to.reason: Grade 5 builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

skills.name: Elewa ujumbe wa kifungu cha hadithi
skills.mastery: Answers who, what and which questions from a short story, puts four events in order, and gives the main message, without choosing a detail for the message or an answer from outside the story, in 8 of 10 new questions.

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.
Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.
Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

leads_to.reason: Grade 5 builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

misconceptions.error: Picks a word that looks or sounds like the word.

example.question: Katika kifungu, neno "mche" lina maana gani?

misconceptions.cause: The child goes by the first letters.
misconceptions.reveals: A look-alike word as an option.
misconceptions.help: Say what each word means.
misconceptions.feedback: Maneno yanaweza kufanana kwa umbo na yasiwe na maana sawa. Mche ni mmea mchanga wa kupanda, si mchele.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Picks a word from the same sentence, not the word asked.

example.question: Katika kifungu, neno "kuchemsha" lina maana gani?

misconceptions.cause: The child picks the meaning of a nearby action.
misconceptions.reveals: The meaning of the word next to it as an option.
misconceptions.help: Put each meaning in place of the word. Which one fits?
misconceptions.feedback: Jaribu kila maana mahali pa neno hilo. Maana sahihi ndiyo inayofaa sentensi nzima.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Picks the opposite of the word.

example.question: Katika kifungu, neno "madonge" lina maana gani?

misconceptions.cause: The child knows what the word is about but not which way it points.
misconceptions.reveals: The opposite meaning as an option.
misconceptions.help: Read the sentence again: does it say the thing is there or not?
misconceptions.feedback: Maana ya neno hutegemea sentensi lilimotumika. Madonge ni vipande vilivyoshikana, si unga laini.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Names the wrong person from the story.

example.question: Nani alimwita Achieng sokoni?

misconceptions.cause: The child goes by the name that comes first in the passage.
misconceptions.reveals: A question about who, with other people in the story.
misconceptions.help: Find the sentence that names the person who did it.
misconceptions.feedback: Kifungu kinasema nani alifanya kitendo hicho. Soma sentensi hiyo tena.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives an answer from what the child knows, not from the passage.

example.question: Achieng alinunua nini sokoni?

misconceptions.cause: The child answers from life and does not look in the text.
misconceptions.reveals: A likely answer that the story does not give.
misconceptions.help: Point to the sentence in the passage that says it.
misconceptions.feedback: Jibu la swali la ufahamu liko kwenye kifungu. Tafuta sentensi inayolisema.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Picks another detail from the story.

example.question: Mvua ilinyesha lini?

misconceptions.cause: The child picks a detail from the right place but not the one asked.
misconceptions.reveals: Several details from one sentence.
misconceptions.help: Read the question word again: who, when, where, what?
misconceptions.feedback: Maneno ya swali (nani, lini, wapi, nini) yanaonyesha jibu la aina gani. Soma kifungu tena.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives a detail for the main message.

example.question: Ujumbe mkuu wa hadithi ni upi?

misconceptions.cause: The child takes the most vivid detail.
misconceptions.reveals: A detail and a message as options.
misconceptions.help: What did the story want us to learn?
misconceptions.feedback: Ujumbe mkuu ni funzo la hadithi nzima, si jambo moja dogo ndani yake.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Puts the events in the wrong order.

example.question: Matukio manne yamechanganywa. Yalitokea kwa mpangilio gani?

misconceptions.cause: The child goes by the order in the question and not in the story.
misconceptions.reveals: Four events shown out of order.
misconceptions.help: Find the first event, then the next.
misconceptions.feedback: Hadithi inasimulia matukio kwa mpangilio. Maneno kama "kisha" na "baadaye" husaidia.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives the English word as the meaning, or a word from the mother tongue, instead of a Kiswahili explanation.

example.question: Katika kifungu, "sebule" maana yake ni nini?
example.correct_answer: chumba cha kukaa na kupokea wageni

misconceptions.cause: The child translates in his head and writes what he thought.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Katika kifungu, "sebule" maana yake ni nini?" with "sitting room" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask for the meaning in Kiswahili words; use a picture of the room to talk about it.
misconceptions.feedback: Eleza maana kwa Kiswahili: sebule ni chumba cha kukaa na wageni.
misconceptions.source: English or mother-tongue interference on Kiswahili; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

learning_experiences: kujadili na wenzake maana ya insha ya wasifu,
kutambua insha ya wasifu kwa kurejelea vielelezo vya insha vilivyoandikwa kwenye matini mbalimbali au tarakilishi,
kujadili na wenzake mada ya insha na muundo wa insha ya wasifu,
kuandaa vidokezo vitakavyomwongoza kuandika insha yake,

kuandika insha inayoeleza sifa za mtu kama vile mzazi au mlezi, rafiki, mwalimu au kiongozi yeyote kwa kuzingatia anwani, mpangilio mzuri wa mawazo, hati nadhifu, tahajia, kanuni za kisarufi, uakifishaji mwafaka na kwa ubunifu,
kuandika insha ya wasifu mtandaoni na kuisambaza kwa wenzake na mwalimu ili waisome na kuitathmini.
key_inquiry_questions: Je, unazingatia mambo gani unapoandika insha nzuri ya wasifu?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhiriki katika mijadala na kazi za vikundi kujadili mada na muundo wa insha ya wasifu.
Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anapotumia kifaa cha kidijitali kuandika na kusambaza insha ya wasifu mtandaoni.
Ubunifu: mwanafunzi anapoandika insha ya wasifu.
Kujiamini: mwanafunzi anapoweza kuandika insha ya wasifu kwa kuzingatia anwani, mpangilio mzuri wa mawazo, hati nadhifu, tahajia, kanuni za kisarufi, uakifishaji mwafaka.
sub_strands.values:
Heshima: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake kujadili mada na muundo wa insha ya wasifu.
Uwajibikaji: mwanafunzi anapotumia kifaa cha kidijitali kuandika insha na kukitunza.
sub_strands.pcis:
Mshikamano wa kijamii: mwanafunzi anapofanya shughuli za kikundi pamoja na wenzake kwa amani.
Haki za watoto: mwanafunzi anaposoma masuala kuhusu mambo ya nyumbani katika insha au kifungu.
sub_strands.links: Mwanafunzi anaweza kuhusisha stadi ya kuandika insha ya wasifu katika somo hili na ujifunzaji wa dhana hiyo katika somo la English.

outcomes.text: kutambua insha ya wasifu kwa kuzingatia muundo
kuandika insha ya wasifu kwa kuzingatia ujumbe, mtindo na muundo ufaao
kuchangamkia utunzi mzuri wa insha ya wasifu ili kujenga ubunifu wake

skills.name: Tambua insha ya wasifu, masimulizi na maelezo na sehemu za insha
skills.mastery: Names the kind of insha from a short text (wasifu describes a person or thing, masimulizi tells what happened in order, maelezo explains) and the part of an insha (utangulizi, kiini, hitimisho), in 8 of 10 new items.

prerequisites.reason: The things to keep in mind when writing an insha were met in Grade 3.
A Grade 3 maelezo is one of the kinds the child now sorts.

leads_to.reason: Grade 5 builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

skills.name: Tambua na andika insha ya wasifu
skills.mastery: Tells insha ya wasifu from other kinds of writing and its parts, and writes a description of a person, place or thing with describing words that agree with their nouns and no story of events; the teacher marks the writing with the KICD rubric, and in the app the child picks the right sentence, order or part in 8 of 10 new items.

prerequisites.reason: Telling the kinds of insha and their parts comes before writing one.
The things to keep in mind when writing an insha were met in Grade 3.

misconceptions.error: Calls a text that describes a person or thing a masimulizi.

example.question: Ni insha ya aina gani? "Bibi yangu ni mpole. Ana nywele nyeupe na anapenda kusimulia hadithi."

misconceptions.cause: The child sees that it is about a person and thinks of a story.
misconceptions.reveals: A description of a person.
misconceptions.help: Does the text tell what happened in order, or what the person is like?
misconceptions.feedback: Wasifu humwelezea mtu au kitu: sura, tabia na maisha. Masimulizi husimulia matukio kwa mpangilio.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Calls a text that tells what happened a wasifu.

example.question: Ni insha ya aina gani? "Jumamosi, Achieng alienda sokoni. Mvua ilianza kunyesha, akakimbilia dukani."

misconceptions.cause: The child sees a person and thinks it describes her.
misconceptions.reveals: A story about a person.
misconceptions.help: Is something happening, one thing after another?
misconceptions.feedback: Masimulizi husimulia mambo yaliyotokea kwa mpangilio. Wasifu huelezea jinsi mtu alivyo.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Calls a text that explains how to do something a masimulizi.

example.question: Ni insha ya aina gani? "Ili kupika wali, osha mchele kwanza. Kisha chemsha maji."

misconceptions.cause: The child sees steps and reads them as events.
misconceptions.reveals: Instructions that sound like a story.
misconceptions.help: Is it telling what happened, or how to do it?
misconceptions.feedback: Maelezo hueleza jambo au jinsi ya kufanya kitu hatua kwa hatua.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Mixes the parts of an insha (utangulizi, kiini, hitimisho).

example.question: Sehemu ya mwisho ya insha huitwa ___.

misconceptions.cause: The child knows the three names but not their order.
misconceptions.reveals: The three parts asked in turn.
misconceptions.help: Which part comes first, which in the middle, which last?
misconceptions.feedback: Insha ina utangulizi mwanzoni, kiini katikati na hitimisho mwishoni.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Tells a story of what happened where the insha should describe the person, place or thing.

example.question: Ni sentensi ipi inafaa katika insha ya wasifu kuhusu "Nyumbani Kwetu"?
example.correct_answer: Nyumba yetu ina paa jekundu na madirisha manne makubwa.

misconceptions.cause: Stories are the kind of writing the child has done most and he falls back on it.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni sentensi ipi inafaa katika insha ya wasifu kuhusu "Nyumbani Kwetu"?" with "Siku moja tulienda sokoni tukapotea." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask what the reader should know about the topic at the end: what it looks like, what it is for.
misconceptions.feedback: Insha ya wasifu hueleza jinsi kitu au mtu alivyo, si matukio ya siku moja.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Describes with empty words (kizuri sana, kibaya) and no detail that makes a picture.

example.question: Ni sentensi ipi inajenga picha dhahiri kuhusu "Nyumbani Kwetu"?
example.correct_answer: Nyumba yetu ina paa jekundu na madirisha manne makubwa.

misconceptions.cause: The child knows the thing well and assumes the reader sees it too.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni sentensi ipi inajenga picha dhahiri kuhusu "Nyumbani Kwetu"?" with "Nyumba yetu ni nzuri sana." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Five senses chart: what do you see, hear, smell, touch, taste? Turn one row into a sentence.
misconceptions.feedback: Tumia vivumishi na maelezo ya rangi, umbo, ukubwa na sauti ili msomaji aone picha.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Uses a describing word that does not agree with its noun (bendera mzuri, miti mrefu).

example.question: Ni sentensi ipi ni sahihi?
example.wrong_answer: Nyumba yetu ina vyumba vitatu mikubwa.
example.correct_answer: Nyumba yetu ina vyumba vitatu vikubwa.

misconceptions.cause: The child uses one form of the adjective (m-) for every noun, as he hears it for people.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni sentensi ipi ni sahihi?" with "Nyumba yetu ina vyumba vitatu mikubwa." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Find the noun first, then its ngeli, then the prefix of the adjective.
misconceptions.feedback: Kivumishi hupatana na nomino yake: bendera nzuri, miti mirefu, mtoto mzuri.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Puts in points that are not about the title.

example.question: Katika insha ya wasifu yenye anwani "Nyumbani Kwetu", ni sentensi ipi haifai?
example.wrong_answer: Rafiki yangu ana baiskeli mpya ya rangi ya bluu.
example.correct_answer: Nyumba yetu ina paa jekundu na madirisha manne makubwa.

misconceptions.cause: The child adds whatever he remembers so the insha is long enough.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Katika insha ya wasifu yenye anwani "Nyumbani Kwetu", ni sentensi ipi haifai?" with "Rafiki yangu ana baiskeli mpya ya rangi ya bluu." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Read each sentence and ask: does it tell the reader about the title? Cross out the ones that do not.
misconceptions.feedback: Kila sentensi ya insha inapaswa kuhusu anwani.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

learning_experiences: kushirikiana na wenzake kueleza maana ya nomino,

skills.name: Tambua na tumia nomino
skills.mastery: Picks the noun (the name of a person, animal, place or thing) from a group of words and a sentence, and fills a gap with a noun, without choosing a verb, an adjective or an adverb, in 8 of 10 new items.

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.
Changing a sentence from one to many shows which word is the name that changes.
Knowing words for people, animals and things of a theme gives the child nouns to sort.

leads_to.reason: Grade 5 builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.
Grade 5 builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

misconceptions.error: Picks a verb (a word for an action) for a noun.

example.question: Mama ananunua ___ sokoni.

misconceptions.cause: The child sees a word that goes with the sentence and does not ask what kind of word it is.
misconceptions.reveals: A gap that needs a thing, with a verb among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask: is it the name of something, or something being done?
misconceptions.feedback: Nomino ni jina la mtu, mnyama, mahali au kitu. "Anapika" ni kitenzi, kinaonyesha kitendo.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Picks an adjective (a word that describes) for a noun.

example.question: Ni neno lipi ni nomino?

misconceptions.cause: The child picks the word that tells about the thing, not the thing.
misconceptions.reveals: A noun among describing words.
misconceptions.help: Can you hold it, see it or name it? Then it may be a noun.
misconceptions.feedback: Nomino ni jina la kitu chenyewe. "Kubwa" ni kivumishi, kinaeleza kitu kikoje.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Picks a word of time or manner (haraka, jana, sana) for a noun.

example.question: Ni neno lipi ni nomino?

misconceptions.cause: The child picks a short word that fits the sentence.
misconceptions.reveals: A noun among words of time and manner.
misconceptions.help: Does the word name something?
misconceptions.feedback: "Haraka" na "jana" ni vielezi: vinaonyesha jinsi au wakati. Nomino hutaja mtu, mnyama, mahali au kitu.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Picks a pronoun (yeye, wao, huyu) as the noun in the sentence.

example.question: Ni nomino ipi katika sentensi: "Yeye alimpa mtoto chakula"?

misconceptions.cause: A pronoun stands where a noun stands, so the child takes it for one.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni nomino ipi katika sentensi: "Yeye alimpa mtoto chakula"?" with "Yeye" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask: does the word name someone or something, or does it point to someone already named?
misconceptions.feedback: Yeye ni kiwakilishi: kinasimama badala ya jina. Nomino ni jina: mtoto, chakula.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhiriki katika mijadala, kazi za vikundi na mawasiliano mtandaoni.

skills.name: Tambua na tumia vitenzi
skills.mastery: Picks the verb (the word for what someone or something does) from a group of words and a sentence, and fills a gap with a verb, without choosing a noun, an adjective or an adverb, in 8 of 10 new items.

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.
Making a sentence negative changes the verb, which shows the child where the verb is.

leads_to.reason: Grade 5 builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.
Grade 5 builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

misconceptions.error: Picks a noun for a verb.

example.question: Juma ___ mpira uwanjani.

misconceptions.cause: The child takes the word nearest the gap that names a thing.
misconceptions.reveals: A gap that needs an action, with a noun among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask: what is Juma doing?
misconceptions.feedback: Kitenzi kinaonyesha kitendo: anacheza. "Uwanja" ni nomino, ni jina la mahali.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Picks an adjective for a verb.

example.question: Mama ___ chakula jikoni.

misconceptions.cause: The child picks a word that goes with chakula.
misconceptions.reveals: A gap that needs an action, with a describing word among the options.
misconceptions.help: Can you do the word? Cooking can be done; "kitamu" cannot.
misconceptions.feedback: Kitenzi kinaonyesha kitendo. "Kitamu" ni kivumishi, kinaeleza chakula kikoje.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Picks a word of time or manner (sasa, mapema) for a verb.

example.question: Wakulima ___ mahindi shambani.

misconceptions.cause: The child picks a small word that seems to fit.
misconceptions.reveals: A gap that needs an action, with a time or manner word.
misconceptions.help: Ask: who does what?
misconceptions.feedback: "Mapema" ni kielezi cha wakati. Kitenzi ni neno la kitendo, kama "wanapanda".
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Takes the verb-noun with ku- (kusoma ni kuzuri) and the verb in a sentence as different kinds, or calls a verb-noun the verb of the sentence.

example.question: Ni kitenzi kipi katika sentensi: "Kuogelea kunafurahisha"?

misconceptions.cause: Every word with ku- looks like a verb to the child.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni kitenzi kipi katika sentensi: "Kuogelea kunafurahisha"?" with "Kuogelea" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask what the sentence says is happening; the ku- word here is the thing being talked about.
misconceptions.feedback: Kuogelea hapa ni jina la jambo; kitenzi ni kunafurahisha.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

sub_strands.core_competences:

skills.name: Tambua na tumia vivumishi
skills.mastery: Picks the adjective (the word that tells more about a noun) and uses the form that agrees with the noun (mtoto mdogo, watoto wadogo, kiti kikubwa), without choosing a noun or a verb, in 8 of 10 new items.

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.
Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

misconceptions.error: Picks a noun for an adjective.

example.question: Mtoto ___ anacheza uwanjani.

misconceptions.cause: The child picks a word for a person.
misconceptions.reveals: A gap that needs a describing word, with a noun among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask: does the word tell what kind of child?
misconceptions.feedback: Kivumishi kinaeleza nomino ikoje, kama "mdogo". "Mwalimu" ni nomino.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Picks a verb for an adjective.

example.question: Nyumba ___ ina bustani.

misconceptions.cause: The child fills the gap with any word that fits the meaning.
misconceptions.reveals: A gap that needs a describing word, with a verb among the options.
misconceptions.help: Does the word tell how the house is, or what it does?
misconceptions.feedback: Kivumishi kinaeleza nomino ikoje: nyumba nzuri. "Inaonekana" ni kitenzi.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Uses an adjective that does not agree with its noun (watoto mdogo, kiti mkubwa).

example.question: Watoto ___ wanacheza.

misconceptions.cause: The child keeps the form of the adjective for one thing.
misconceptions.reveals: Plural and singular nouns in turn, with the same adjective.
misconceptions.help: Count: one or many? The adjective changes with the noun.
misconceptions.feedback: Kivumishi hubadilika kulingana na nomino: mtoto mdogo, watoto wadogo; kiti kikubwa, viti vikubwa.
misconceptions.source: English or mother-tongue influence on Kiswahili (to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher)

misconceptions.error: Puts the describing word before the noun, as in English (mzuri mtoto, kubwa nyumba).

example.question: Ni ipi ni sahihi?

misconceptions.cause: In English the adjective comes first, and the child carries that order over.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni ipi ni sahihi?" with "mzuri mtoto" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Say noun first, then the word that describes it; build phrases with two cards that must be in order.
misconceptions.feedback: Katika Kiswahili, nomino hutangulia kivumishi: mtoto mzuri, nyumba kubwa.
misconceptions.source: English or mother-tongue interference on Kiswahili; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Tambua maamkuzi na maagano katika miktadha mbalimbali
skills.mastery: Picks the greeting or farewell that fits the person and the time (hujambo-sijambo, shikamoo-marahaba, habari za asubuhi, kwaheri, usiku mwema), without giving the greeting back as the reply, in 8 of 10 new situations. Using them aloud is a teacher's check.

prerequisites.reason: The everyday greetings and farewells of Grade 3 come first.
Shikamoo and marahaba are words of respect met in Grade 3.

leads_to.reason: Grade 5 builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

misconceptions.error: Gives the greeting back as the reply (Hujambo for Sijambo).

example.question: Mtu akikusalimia "Hujambo?", unajibu "___."

misconceptions.cause: The child repeats the word he heard.
misconceptions.reveals: A greeting and its reply as options.
misconceptions.help: Who is asking, and who answers?
misconceptions.feedback: Hujambo hujibiwa kwa "Sijambo". Shikamoo hujibiwa kwa "Marahaba".
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Uses a greeting of the wrong time of day (habari za asubuhi at night).

example.question: Kabla ya kulala usiku unamwambia mama, "___."

misconceptions.cause: The child knows the greeting but not when it is used.
misconceptions.reveals: A morning greeting for an evening situation.
misconceptions.help: What time of day is it?
misconceptions.feedback: "Habari za asubuhi" ni ya asubuhi. "Usiku mwema" husemwa usiku kabla ya kulala.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Greets an elder with the greeting for a friend (hujambo for shikamoo).

example.question: Unamsalimia babu yako kwa kusema "___."

misconceptions.cause: The child uses one greeting for everyone.
misconceptions.reveals: An elder and a friend as the people greeted.
misconceptions.help: Is the person older than you?
misconceptions.feedback: Mdogo humsalimia mkubwa kwa "Shikamoo", na mkubwa hujibu "Marahaba". "Hujambo" ni ya rika moja.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Uses a greeting where a farewell is needed (Hujambo! when leaving), or the reverse.

example.question: Unaondoka nyumbani kwa shangazi jioni. Unasema nini?

misconceptions.cause: Greeting and farewell words are learnt together on one chart and the child mixes the columns.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Unaondoka nyumbani kwa shangazi jioni. Unasema nini?" with "Hujambo shangazi!" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Act out arriving and leaving at a door; the child says the right word at each.
misconceptions.feedback: Unapoondoka unaaga: Kwaheri, usiku mwema.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Tumia kamusi: mpangilio wa maneno na maana
skills.mastery: Puts words in the order of the alphabet (using the second and third letters when the first match) and says what a dictionary is for, in 8 of 10 new items.

prerequisites.reason: Spelling words letter by letter is needed to look them up.
The dictionary answers the question the passage raised: what does this word mean?

leads_to.reason: Grade 5 builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

misconceptions.error: Looks at the first letter only (words that begin alike).

example.question: Kati ya "samaki", "sahani" na "sufuria", neno linalokuja kwanza ni ___.

misconceptions.cause: The child stops when the first letters are the same.
misconceptions.reveals: Words that begin with the same letter.
misconceptions.help: When the first letters match, look at the second.
misconceptions.feedback: Maneno yakianza kwa herufi moja, tazama herufi ya pili, kisha ya tatu.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Puts the shortest word first.

example.question: Kati ya "ua", "ardhi" na "wali", neno linalokuja kwanza ni ___.

misconceptions.cause: The child orders by how short or long the word is.
misconceptions.reveals: A short word that begins with a late letter.
misconceptions.help: Go by the letters of the alphabet, not by how long the word is.
misconceptions.feedback: Kamusi hupanga maneno kwa mpangilio wa alfabeti, si kwa urefu wa neno.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Goes from z back to a.

example.question: Kati ya "baba", "mto" na "zeze", neno linalokuja kwanza ni ___.

misconceptions.cause: The child reads the alphabet from the end.
misconceptions.reveals: First and last words asked in turn.
misconceptions.help: The alphabet begins with a.
misconceptions.feedback: Alfabeti huanza na a na kuishia na z. Neno lenye herufi ya mwanzo karibu na a hutangulia.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Does not know what a dictionary is for (takes it for a storybook or a book of pictures).

example.question: Kamusi hutusaidia kupata ___ ya neno.

misconceptions.cause: The child has seen a dictionary but not used it.
misconceptions.reveals: The use of a dictionary asked directly.
misconceptions.help: What do you look for when you meet a word you do not know?
misconceptions.feedback: Kamusi ni kitabu chenye maneno na maana zake, yaliyopangwa kwa mpangilio wa alfabeti.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

learning_experiences: kutambua insha ya masimulizi kwa kurejelea vielelezo vya insha zilizoandikwa kwenye matini mbalimbali au tarakilishi,
kushiriki na wenzake kujadili mada ya insha na muundo wa insha ya masimulizi,
kuandaa vidokezo vitakavyomwongoza kuandika insha yake,
kuandika insha inayosimulia kisa kinachohusu nidhamu mezani kwa kuzingatia anwani, mpangilio mzuri wa mawazo, hati safi, tahajia, kanuni za kisarufi, uakifishaji mwafaka na kwa lugha ya kiubunifu,
kuwasomea wenzake insha aliyoandika ili waitathmini.

Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhiriki katika mijadala na kazi za vikundi.
Ubunifu: mwanafunzi anapoandika insha ya masimulizi.
Hamu ya ujifunzaji: mwanafunzi anapoyatafakari maswali dadisi na anapoimarisha ujuzi wake wa kutumia tarakilishi.
sub_strands.values: Heshima: mwanafunzi anapothamini mchango wa wenzake katika kikundi.
sub_strands.pcis: Mshikamano wa kijamii: mwanfunzi anapokuza uraia wema kwa kufanya shughuli ya kikundi na wenzake na kuthamini mchango wao.
sub_strands.links:
Mwanafunzi anaweza kuhusisha dhana ya insha ya masimulizi katika somo hili na ujifunzaji wa dhana hiyo katika somo la English.
Mwanafunzi anaweza kuhusisha suala la nidhamu mezani na masuala yanayofunzwa katika somo la Agriculture.

kuandika insha ya masimulizi inayozingatia mada, ujumbe, mtindo na muundo ufaao

skills.name: Tambua na andika insha ya masimulizi
skills.mastery: Tells insha ya masimulizi from other kinds of writing and its parts, and writes a story of events in the past tense, in order, with a title, an opening, a middle and a closing that gives the lesson; the teacher marks the writing with the KICD rubric, and in the app the child picks the right sentence, order or part in 8 of 10 new items.

prerequisites.reason: Telling the kinds of insha and their parts comes before writing one.
Grade 3 already told a short story in writing.

misconceptions.error: Writes facts or an explanation where a story of events is asked.

example.question: Ni sentensi ipi ni mwanzo wa insha ya masimulizi yenye anwani "Siku Nilipokula na Wageni"?
example.wrong_answer: Watu wengi hula mara tatu kwa siku.
example.correct_answer: Jana jioni tulikula chakula pamoja na wageni wetu.

misconceptions.cause: The child knows a lot about the topic and writes what he knows instead of telling what happened.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni sentensi ipi ni mwanzo wa insha ya masimulizi yenye anwani "Siku Nilipokula na Wageni"?" with "Watu wengi hula mara tatu kwa siku." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask: who, where, what happened first, then, in the end? A story answers these; an explanation does not.
misconceptions.feedback: Masimulizi husimulia matukio yaliyotokea: nani, wapi, nini kilitokea.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Tells a past story in the present tense (-na-), or mixes -na- and -li- in one story.

example.question: Ni sentensi ipi inafaa katika masimulizi ya jambo lililotokea jana: "Siku Nilipokula na Wageni"?
example.wrong_answer: Jana jioni tunakula chakula pamoja na wageni wetu.
example.correct_answer: Jana jioni tulikula chakula pamoja na wageni wetu.

misconceptions.cause: The child writes as he speaks while remembering, and English stories in class are told in the present too.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni sentensi ipi inafaa katika masimulizi ya jambo lililotokea jana: "Siku Nilipokula na Wageni"?" with "Jana jioni tunakula chakula pamoja na wageni wetu." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Circle every verb; check its tense marker against the time words (jana, siku moja).
misconceptions.feedback: Jambo lililotokea husimuliwa kwa wakati uliopita: -li-.
misconceptions.source: English or mother-tongue interference on Kiswahili; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Puts the events in an order that cannot have happened (the end before the start), with no linking words.

example.question: Ni mpangilio upi wa matukio unafaa katika insha "Siku Nilipokula na Wageni"?
example.wrong_answer: tulishukuru, tulikula, tuliketi mezani, tulinawa mikono
example.correct_answer: tulinawa mikono, tuliketi mezani, tulikula, tulishukuru

misconceptions.cause: The child writes events as they come to mind; nobody has asked for a plan first.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni mpangilio upi wa matukio unafaa katika insha "Siku Nilipokula na Wageni"?" with "tulishukuru, tulikula, tuliketi mezani, tulinawa mikono" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Plan with three boxes (mwanzo, kati, mwisho) and linking words (kwanza, kisha, hatimaye) before writing.
misconceptions.feedback: Panga matukio yanavyofuatana, na utumie maneno kama kwanza, kisha na hatimaye.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Ends the insha abruptly ("Mwisho." or "The end") with no closing paragraph (hitimisho).

example.question: Ni ipi ni hitimisho bora la insha "Siku Nilipokula na Wageni"?
example.correct_answer: Tangu siku hiyo, nimejifunza kuwa mwangalifu kila wakati.

misconceptions.cause: Storybooks for young readers end with "Mwisho" and the child copies that.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni ipi ni hitimisho bora la insha "Siku Nilipokula na Wageni"?" with "Mwisho." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Show three endings; the child picks the one that closes the main idea or the lesson.
misconceptions.feedback: Hitimisho hufunga insha kwa kueleza funzo au hisia, si kwa neno "Mwisho" tu.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhiriki katika mijadala, kazi za vikundi na mawasiliano mtandaoni.

Heshima: mwanafunzi anapothamini mchango wa wenzake katika shughuli za kikundi.

skills.name: Tambua na tumia viwakilishi
skills.mastery: Picks the pronoun (the word that stands in place of a noun: yeye, wao, sisi, huyu, hawa, yule, wale) that fits the person, number and nearness, without repeating the noun or choosing another word, in 8 of 10 new items.

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.
Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.
Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

misconceptions.error: Repeats the noun instead of using a pronoun.

example.question: Wanjiru ni msichana. ___ anapenda kusoma.

misconceptions.cause: The child does not see that a pronoun stands in place of the name.
misconceptions.reveals: A second sentence that needs a pronoun, with the name among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask: which word saves us saying the name again?
misconceptions.feedback: Kiwakilishi husimama mahali pa nomino ili tusirudie jina: "Yeye" badala ya "Wanjiru".
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Uses a pronoun for one where there are many, or for many where there is one (yeye for wao).

example.question: Juma na Otieno ni marafiki. ___ wanacheza pamoja.

misconceptions.cause: The child does not count the people.
misconceptions.reveals: A pair of people with a one-person pronoun among the options.
misconceptions.help: Count the people. One is "yeye", many are "wao".
misconceptions.feedback: "Yeye" ni mtu mmoja. "Wao" ni watu wengi. Juma na Otieno ni wawili, kwa hiyo ni "wao".
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Swaps the person (mimi, wewe, yeye, sisi, nyinyi, wao).

example.question: Mimi na wewe ni marafiki. ___ tunasoma pamoja.

misconceptions.cause: The child knows the pronouns but not who is speaking.
misconceptions.reveals: A sentence about the speaker and the listener.
misconceptions.help: Does it include me, the speaker?
misconceptions.feedback: "Sisi" ni mimi na wengine. "Wao" ni watu wengine, bila mimi.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Swaps the near and the far one (huyu for yule, hawa for wale).

example.question: Angalia, ___ ni mwalimu wetu, ameketi karibu nami.

misconceptions.cause: The child does not take the distance into account.
misconceptions.reveals: A person who is close and a person who is far, with both words as options.
misconceptions.help: Is the person near you or far from you?
misconceptions.feedback: "Huyu" na "hawa" hutumika kwa walio karibu. "Yule" na "wale" hutumika kwa walio mbali.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Tambua na tumia vielezi
skills.mastery: Picks the adverb (the word that tells how, when or where something is done: polepole, jana, shuleni) and says which of the three it tells, without choosing an adjective or a noun, in 8 of 10 new items.

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.
Telling a word that describes a noun from one that describes an action needs both kinds side by side.

misconceptions.error: Uses an adjective for an adverb (anaimba nzuri for anaimba vizuri).

example.question: Wanafunzi wanaimba ___ darasani.

misconceptions.cause: The child uses the describing word of a noun for the way something is done.
misconceptions.reveals: A gap that tells how something is done, with the adjective among the options.
misconceptions.help: Does it tell how they sing, or what kind of thing it is?
misconceptions.feedback: Kielezi kinaonyesha jinsi kitendo kinavyofanyika: wanaimba vizuri. "Nzuri" ni kivumishi cha nomino.
misconceptions.source: English or mother-tongue influence on Kiswahili (to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher)

misconceptions.error: Picks a noun for an adverb.

example.question: Mtoto alikimbia ___ kuelekea nyumbani.

misconceptions.cause: The child picks a word of the place and not the way.
misconceptions.reveals: A gap that tells how something is done, with a noun among the options.
misconceptions.help: Does the word tell how he ran?
misconceptions.feedback: "Haraka" ni kielezi cha jinsi. "Barabara" ni nomino.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Mixes the three kinds of adverb (time, place, manner).

example.question: Kielezi "jana" kinaonyesha ___.

misconceptions.cause: The child knows the word is an adverb but not what it tells.
misconceptions.reveals: Adverbs of time, place and manner asked in turn.
misconceptions.help: Ask: does it tell when, where or how?
misconceptions.feedback: Vielezi vya wakati (jana, kesho), mahali (hapa, mbali) na jinsi (polepole, haraka) vinajibu "lini", "wapi" na "vipi".
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Takes a place word (nyumbani, shuleni) for a noun, not an adverb of place, in a sentence.

example.question: Neno "shuleni" katika "Tunasoma shuleni" ni nini?

misconceptions.cause: The child sees the noun shule inside the word and stops there.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno "shuleni" katika "Tunasoma shuleni" ni nini?" with "nomino" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask what question the word answers: wapi? lini? vipi? The -ni ending turns the noun into a place word.
misconceptions.feedback: Shuleni hujibu swali "wapi?": ni kielezi cha mahali.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

learning_experiences: kutafiti maana ya kitendawili kwenye kamusi, vitabuni au mtandaoni akiwa na wenzake,

Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anapotumia vyombo vya kidijitali kusikiliza vitendawili vikitegwa na kuteguliwa.
Kujiamini: mwanafunzi anapotega na kutegua vitendawili ipasavyo.

Heshima: mwanafunzi anachangamkia maoni ya wenzake darasani.

sub_strands.pcis: Umoja wa kijamii: mwanafunzi anapofanya kazi ya kutega na kutegua vitendawili pamoja na wenzake katika kikundi.

kutega na kutegua vitendawili ili kukuza uwazaji kina

skills.name: Tambua vitendawili
skills.mastery: Tells a kitendawili from a methali, a nahau and an ordinary sentence, gives the opening words of riddling (Kitendawili! Tega!), and the answer to a known riddle, in 8 of 10 new items. Telling and guessing aloud is a teacher's check.

prerequisites.reason: The answer to a riddle is almost always a noun.
Vocabulary of everyday things gives the child the answers to guess.

leads_to.reason: Grade 5 builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

misconceptions.error: Takes a methali for a riddle.

example.question: Ni kitendawili kipi?

misconceptions.cause: Both are short sayings.
misconceptions.reveals: A riddle and a methali.
misconceptions.help: A riddle hides an answer. Can you guess it?
misconceptions.feedback: Kitendawili huficha jibu na humtaka mtu kukitegua. Methali hutoa funzo.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Takes a nahau for a riddle.

example.question: Ni kitendawili kipi?

misconceptions.cause: Both can be a short phrase.
misconceptions.reveals: A riddle and a nahau.
misconceptions.help: Can you give an answer to it?
misconceptions.feedback: Nahau ni maneno yenye maana maalum. Kitendawili kina jibu la kutegua.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Takes an ordinary sentence for a riddle.

example.question: Ni kitendawili kipi?

misconceptions.cause: The child does not see that a riddle hides the thing it describes.
misconceptions.reveals: A riddle and a plain sentence.
misconceptions.help: Does the text name the thing, or hide it?
misconceptions.feedback: Kitendawili hakitaji kitu moja kwa moja; hukielezea kwa fumbo.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Does not know the words used when riddling (Kitendawili! Tega!).

example.question: Mtegaji husema "Kitendawili!" Mtegua hujibu "___!"

misconceptions.cause: The child has heard a riddle told but not the fixed words.
misconceptions.reveals: The opening and the giving-up words.
misconceptions.help: What does the guesser say to say he is ready?
misconceptions.feedback: Mtegaji husema "Kitendawili!" na mtegua hujibu "Tega!". Akishindwa husema "Nipe mji."
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives a thing that shares one detail with the riddle but is not the answer.

example.question: "Popote niendapo hunifuata." Jibu ni nini?

misconceptions.cause: The child picks the first thing that comes to mind.
misconceptions.reveals: A riddle with plausible answers.
misconceptions.help: Test each answer against every part of the riddle.
misconceptions.feedback: Jibu la kitendawili lazima lilingane na kila sehemu yake.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Tambua vipengele vya kusoma kwa ufasaha
skills.mastery: Names what a fluent reader does (good pronunciation, a fitting voice, a fitting speed, a rest at the marks, signs that fit), without taking fast or loud for good, in 8 of 10 new items. Reading aloud itself is for a teacher to hear.
question_forms: choose what a good reader does

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.
Reading for meaning is what fluent reading serves.

leads_to.reason: Grade 5 builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

skills.name: Soma kifungu kwa sauti kwa matamshi bora, kasi ifaayo, sauti ifaayo na ishara
skills.mastery: Reads a short passage aloud at a speaking pace, pauses at the koma and the kikomo, raises the voice for a question and shows feeling for an exclamation, says every sound clearly (no l for r), and uses a matching gesture, judged by the teacher with the KICD rubric; in the app picks the better reading of a line in 8 of 10 new items.

prerequisites.reason: Knowing what fluent reading is (pace, voice, marks) comes before doing it.
Grade 3 reading of a short passage with correct sounds is the base.

misconceptions.error: Thinks that reading fast is reading well.

example.question: Ni nini kinachoonyesha kusoma kwa ufasaha?

misconceptions.cause: The child hears that good readers are quick.
misconceptions.reveals: Fast and fitting as options.
misconceptions.help: Can the listener follow every word?
misconceptions.feedback: Kasi ifaayo si haraka sana wala polepole sana: msikilizaji aelewe kila neno.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks that reading loud is reading well.

example.question: Sauti ipasavyo wakati wa kusoma ni ipi?

misconceptions.cause: The child takes loud for clear.
misconceptions.reveals: Loud and clear as options.
misconceptions.help: Is a shout the same as a clear voice?
misconceptions.feedback: Sauti ipasavyo inasikika wazi bila kupiga kelele wala kunong'ona.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Ignores the koma and the kikomo.

example.question: Ukifika kwenye koma, ufanye nini?

misconceptions.cause: The child reads the words and skips the marks.
misconceptions.reveals: A mark that asks for a rest.
misconceptions.help: What does the mark tell the reader to do?
misconceptions.feedback: Alama za uakifishi zinaonyesha mahali pa kupumzika: koma kidogo, kikomo muda mrefu zaidi.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads word by word or syllable by syllable, so the sentence has no meaning when heard.

example.question: Ni usomaji upi ni wa ufasaha: "Mama alinunua sare mpya ya shule sokoni."?
example.wrong_answer: Mama ... alinunua ... sare ... mpya ... ya ... shule ... sokoni.
example.correct_answer: Mama alinunua sare mpya ya shule sokoni.

misconceptions.cause: The child is still decoding each word and has not yet learnt to read a phrase as one piece.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni usomaji upi ni wa ufasaha: "Mama alinunua sare mpya ya shule sokoni."?" with "Mama ... alinunua ... sare ... mpya ... ya ... shule ... sokoni." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Echo reading: the teacher reads a phrase, the child repeats it as one breath; then phrase-cut the passage with slashes.
misconceptions.feedback: Usomaji wa ufasaha husoma kundi la maneno kwa pamoja, kama tunavyozungumza.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads as fast as possible and thinks the fastest reader is the best.

example.question: Ni kasi ipi ifaayo ya kusoma kifungu darasani?
example.correct_answer: kasi ya kuzungumza, ili kila neno lisikike

misconceptions.cause: Reading races in class reward speed; the child has not been asked whether listeners understood.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni kasi ipi ifaayo ya kusoma kifungu darasani?" with "haraka iwezekanavyo" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Time two readings: one very fast, one at speaking pace; listeners answer one question after each.
misconceptions.feedback: Kasi ifaayo ni ile ya kuzungumza: si haraka mno, si polepole mno.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads a question and an exclamation in the same flat voice as a statement.

example.question: Sentensi "Je, umevaa koti lako leo?" inasomwa vipi?
example.wrong_answer: kwa sauti ileile ya sentensi ya kawaida
example.correct_answer: sauti hupanda mwishoni kwa sababu ni swali

misconceptions.cause: The child looks at the words and not at the mark at the end.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Sentensi "Je, umevaa koti lako leo?" inasomwa vipi?" with "kwa sauti ileile ya sentensi ya kawaida" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Read the same words three ways (. ? !); the child points at the mark that matches each reading.
misconceptions.feedback: Kiulizi (?) hupandisha sauti mwishoni; alama ya hisi (!) huonyesha hisia.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads on through the koma and the kikomo without a pause.

example.question: Unasoma: "Lo, viatu vyako vinang'aa sana!" Unasimama wapi kidogo?
example.wrong_answer: hapana mahali, unasoma moja kwa moja
example.correct_answer: kwenye koma na kwenye kikomo au alama ya hisi

misconceptions.cause: The marks are read as decoration; the child has not linked them to breath.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Unasoma: "Lo, viatu vyako vinang'aa sana!" Unasimama wapi kidogo?" with "hapana mahali, unasoma moja kwa moja" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Clap once at a koma, twice at a kikomo while reading together.
misconceptions.feedback: Simama kidogo kwenye koma, na zaidi kwenye kikomo.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Says /l/ for /r/ or /r/ for /l/ while reading (rangi read as langi).

example.question: Neno "rangi" linatamkwa vipi?

misconceptions.cause: The first language of the child does not separate these sounds, so the reading carries the home sound.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno "rangi" linatamkwa vipi?" with "langi" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Make a list of the passage words with the hard sound; practise them before reading the passage.
misconceptions.feedback: Tamka "rangi" kama lilivyoandikwa; "langi" ni neno jingine au si neno.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks gestures and looking up at the listeners have nothing to do with reading well.

example.question: Ni kipi ni kipengele cha kusoma kwa ufasaha?
example.wrong_answer: kuangalia kitabu tu bila kuwaangalia wasikilizaji
example.correct_answer: kuambatanisha ishara na kuwaangalia wasikilizaji mara kwa mara

misconceptions.cause: Reading has only been practised silently or with eyes on the page.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni kipi ni kipengele cha kusoma kwa ufasaha?" with "kuangalia kitabu tu bila kuwaangalia wasikilizaji" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Watch a good reader: list what the body does as well as the voice.
misconceptions.feedback: Msomaji mzuri huwaangalia wasikilizaji na kutumia ishara zifaazo.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

learning_experiences: kutambua sehemu za kimsingi za tarakilishi za kupigia chapa akiwa na wenzake (k.v kiibodi, kipanya, kiwambo, kitufe na faili),
kuzingatia hatua za kufungua na kufunga tarakilishi,
kuandika suala lengwa kwa kutumia tarakilishi akizingatia chapa koza, italiki na kupigia mistari panapofaa,
kuandika aya kuhusu mavazi katika tarakilishi na kuihariri,
kutumia mtandao kusambaza kazi aliyoandika ili wenzake na mwalimu waitathmini,
kuhifadhi kazi yake kwenye faili ya tarakilishi.
key_inquiry_questions: Je, unazingatia nini unapoandika kwa kutumia tarakilishi?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika vikundi.
Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anapotumia tarakilishi kuandika na kuhifadhi kazi yake kwenye faili.
Hamu ya ujifunzaji: mwanafunzi anapotagusana na vyombo vya kidijitali kama vile kutumia tarakilishi na kipakatalishi.
sub_strands.values:
Ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anapotambua sehemu za kimsingi za tarakilishi za kupiga chapa akiwa na wenzake.
Uwajibikaji: mwanafunzi anaweza kutumia na kuhifadhi vifaa vya kidijitali ifaavyo.
sub_strands.pcis: Usalama wa mtandaoni: mwanafunzi anapotumia vifaa vya kidijitali anazingatia kuingia mitandaoni iliyo salama.
sub_strands.links:
Mwanafunzi anaweza kuhusisha dhana ya matumizi ya tarakilishi katika somo hili na ujifunzaji wa dhana hiyo katika somo la Science and Technology.
Mwanafunzi anaweza kuhusisha suala la mavazi na masuala yanayofunzwa katika somo la Social studies.

outcomes.text: kutambua sehemu mbalimbali za tarakilishi zinazotumika kupigia chapa
kufungua na kufunga tarakilishi ili kuandika kazi na kuihifadhi
kuandika suala lengwa kwa kutumia tarakilishi
kuhariri kazi yake kwa kuzingatia uakifishaji ufaao
kuhifadhi kazi aliyoiandika kwenye tarakilishi
kujenga mazoea ya kuandika kwa kutumia tarakilishi na kuhifadhi kazi yake ya maandishi

skills.name: Tambua sehemu za tarakilishi zinazotumika kupigia chapa
skills.mastery: Names the part of a computer for typing and showing (kibodi, kipanya, skrini, kichapishi, the space key) and what each one does, in 8 of 10 new items. Using the computer is a practical task.

prerequisites.reason: Following simple instructions in class is how the parts are learnt.
Spacing on paper is mirrored by the space bar.

leads_to.reason: Grade 5 builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

skills.name: Hariri sentensi: herufi kubwa, kikomo, kiulizi, koma na alama ya hisi
skills.mastery: Chooses the sentence with the right capital letter, kikomo (full stop), kiulizi (question mark), koma and alama ya hisi (!), and finds the one mistake in a short note, in 8 of 10 new sentences.

prerequisites.reason: Grade 3 recognised capital letters in a text.
Grade 3 met the kiulizi.

leads_to.reason: Grade 5 builds on this skill. Proposed, to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

skills.name: Fungua tarakilishi, andika kazi na uihifadhi
skills.mastery: Switches the computer on and off in the right way, opens a word processor, types a short text on the theme with spaces and capital letters, and saves it with a clear file name where he can find it again, in 8 of 10 new items or tasks.

prerequisites.reason: The keyboard, mouse and screen must be known before typing.
Capital letters met in neat handwriting are typed with the shift key.

misconceptions.error: Mixes the parts of a computer (kibodi, kipanya, skrini).

example.question: Tunatumia ___ kupigia herufi na nambari.

misconceptions.cause: The child knows the names but not what each is.
misconceptions.reveals: Parts asked by what they are used for.
misconceptions.help: What do you hold, press or look at?
misconceptions.feedback: Kibodi ina vitufe vya herufi na nambari. Kipanya husogeza kielekezi. Skrini huonyesha. Kichapishi huchapisha.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives the use of another part.

example.question: Skrini hufanya nini?

misconceptions.cause: The child has the right word for the wrong job.
misconceptions.reveals: The use of the part asked in turn.
misconceptions.help: What do you do with this part?
misconceptions.feedback: Kila sehemu ya tarakilishi ina kazi yake: skrini huonyesha, kichapishi huchapisha kwenye karatasi.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Starts a sentence or a name with a small letter.

example.question: Chagua sentensi sahihi.

misconceptions.cause: The child does not see the first letter.
misconceptions.reveals: The same sentence with a small and a capital letter.
misconceptions.help: What do we write first in a sentence?
misconceptions.feedback: Sentensi huanza kwa herufi kubwa, na majina ya pekee pia: Wanjiru, Nairobi.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Ends a question with a kikomo (.) instead of a kiulizi (?).

example.question: Chagua sentensi sahihi.

misconceptions.cause: The child ends every sentence with a full stop.
misconceptions.reveals: The same question with different marks.
misconceptions.help: Is the sentence asking?
misconceptions.feedback: Sentensi ya swali huisha kwa kiulizi (?). Sentensi ya kawaida huisha kwa kikomo (.).
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Leaves out the koma in a list, or puts it in the wrong place.

example.question: Chagua sentensi sahihi.

misconceptions.cause: The child does not pause the sentence where the list items end.
misconceptions.reveals: A list with and without koma.
misconceptions.help: Where would you rest your voice?
misconceptions.feedback: Koma hutenganisha vitu katika orodha: maembe, machungwa na ndizi.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Uses the wrong mark for a feeling (alama ya hisi !) or for a question.

example.question: Chagua sentensi sahihi.

misconceptions.cause: The child does not tell a feeling from a question.
misconceptions.reveals: An exclamation with ! and ?.
misconceptions.help: Is it asking, or showing a feeling?
misconceptions.feedback: Alama ya hisi (!) huonyesha hisia kama furaha au mshangao: Hongera! Kiulizi (?) huuliza.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Leaves out the mark at the end of the sentence.

example.question: Chagua sentensi sahihi.

misconceptions.cause: The child stops writing at the last word.
misconceptions.reveals: The same sentence with and without its closing mark.
misconceptions.help: How does a sentence end?
misconceptions.feedback: Kila sentensi huisha kwa alama: kikomo (.), kiulizi (?) au alama ya hisi (!).
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Switches the computer off by pulling the plug or pressing the power button at once, losing the work.

example.question: Umemaliza kazi. Unazimaje tarakilishi?
example.correct_answer: hifadhi kazi, funga programu, kisha zima kupitia menyu

misconceptions.cause: At home a television or radio is switched off at the plug.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Umemaliza kazi. Unazimaje tarakilishi?" with "chomoa waya wa umeme" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Practise the shut-down steps with step cards, then on a real machine.
misconceptions.feedback: Hifadhi kazi kwanza, kisha zima tarakilishi kupitia menyu.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Closes the document without saving, or saves with no name (Document1) where he cannot find it.

example.question: Ni jina lipi bora la faili ya insha yako ya mavazi?

misconceptions.cause: The child does not know that the work disappears or that the name is how he finds it again.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni jina lipi bora la faili ya insha yako ya mavazi?" with "Document1" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Save, close, then reopen the file by its name in front of the class.
misconceptions.feedback: Hifadhi kazi kwa jina linaloeleza kilicho ndani.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Types words without spaces, or presses the space bar many times instead of using Enter for a new line.

example.question: Ni kitufe kipi huanzisha mstari mpya?

misconceptions.cause: The child has not met the job of each big key.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni kitufe kipi huanzisha mstari mpya?" with "kitufe cha nafasi mara nyingi" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Label the space bar, Enter, Shift and Backspace; type one line, then a new one.
misconceptions.feedback: Enter huanzisha mstari mpya; nafasi hutenganisha maneno.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Leaves caps lock on and types the whole text in capitals, or never makes a capital at the start of a sentence.

example.question: Unataka herufi kubwa moja tu mwanzoni mwa sentensi. Unafanya nini?
example.wrong_answer: washa Caps Lock na uandike sentensi yote

misconceptions.cause: The caps lock light is the only way of making capitals the child has seen.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Unataka herufi kubwa moja tu mwanzoni mwa sentensi. Unafanya nini?" with "washa Caps Lock na uandike sentensi yote" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Type one sentence with Shift for the first letter; compare with all capitals.
misconceptions.feedback: Tumia Shift kwa herufi kubwa moja; Caps Lock hufanya herufi zote kuwa kubwa.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Thinks the screen is the computer and the box (kitengo kikuu) only holds the cables.

example.question: Sehemu ipi ya tarakilishi hufanya kazi ya kufikiri na kuhifadhi?

misconceptions.cause: The screen is where everything is seen, so the child takes it for the computer.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Sehemu ipi ya tarakilishi hufanya kazi ya kufikiri na kuhifadhi?" with "skrini" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Switch the screen off while the computer runs; the work is still there.
misconceptions.feedback: Kitengo kikuu ndicho hufanya kazi; skrini huonyesha tu.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Knows the parts only by their English names (mouse, keyboard) and not kipanya and kibodi.

example.question: Kipanya ni sehemu ipi?

misconceptions.cause: The lab and the computer itself use English names.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kipanya ni sehemu ipi?" with "keyboard" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Label the parts in Kiswahili and use only those in class.
misconceptions.feedback: Kwa Kiswahili: kibodi, kipanya, skrini, kitengo kikuu.
misconceptions.source: English or mother-tongue interference on Kiswahili; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

learning_experiences: kushirikiana na wenzake kueleza maana ya viunganishi,
kutambua viunganishi katika kundi la maneno aliyopewa (k.v na, pia, kwa sababu, lakini),
kutafiti vitabuni au mtandaoni ili kutoa mifano mbalimbali ya viunganishi,
kutumia viunganishi kujaza nafasi katika sentensi,
kutumia viunganishi kutunga sentensi daftarini au mtandaoni kwa kuzingatia suala lengwa na masuala mtambuko mbalimbali,
kumsomea mzazi au mlezi wake sentensi alizozitunga.
key_inquiry_questions: Je, kwa nini ni muhimu kutumia viunganishi katika mawasiliano?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhiriki katika mijadala, kazi za vikundi na mawasiliano mtandaoni.
Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anapotumia kifaa cha kidijitali katika kutambua viunganishi na kutunga sentensi mtandaoni.
Kujiamini: mwanafunzi anapofaulu kutambua viunganishi na kuvitungia sentensi sahihi.
sub_strands.values:
Umoja: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake kueleza maana ya viunganishi na kuvitungia sentensi.
Uadilifu: mwanafunzi anapotumia vifaa vya kidijitali kuchagua viunganishi kutoka kwenye kundi la maneno na kuvitia kapuni.
sub_strands.pcis: Umoja wa kijamii: mwanafunzi anapofanya shughuli ya kikundi pamoja na wenzake wa jamii tofauti.
sub_strands.links:
Mwanafunzi anaweza kuhusisha dhana ya viunganishi katika somo hili na ujifunzaji wa dhana hiyo katika somo la English.
Mwanafunzi anaweza kuhusisha suala la mavazi na masuala yanayofunzwa katika somo la Social Studies na Creative Arts.

outcomes.text: kueleza maana ya kiunganishi ili kukibainisha
kutambua viunganishi katika kundi la maneno na sentensi
kutumia viunganishi kwa njia sahihi katika mawasiliano
kuonea fahari matumizi ya viunganishi katika sentensi

skills.name: Tambua na tumia viunganishi
skills.mastery: Picks the joining word (na, pia, kwa sababu, lakini, ili, au) that fits the meaning of two parts of a sentence, without choosing a noun or a verb or a joining word of another meaning, in 8 of 10 new items.

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.
Joining two nouns (na) is the first use of a joining word.

misconceptions.error: Picks a joining word of another meaning (kwa sababu for lakini, ili for au).

example.question: Alitaka kuogelea, ___ ziwa lilikuwa na mawimbi makali.

misconceptions.cause: The child picks a joining word without asking how the two parts are related.
misconceptions.reveals: Two parts that are in contrast, with the reason word among the options.
misconceptions.help: Do the two parts agree, or does the second go against the first?
misconceptions.feedback: Kila kiunganishi kina kazi: "lakini" kinaonyesha kinyume, "kwa sababu" kinatoa sababu, "ili" kinaonyesha kusudi, "na" kinaongeza.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Picks a noun or a verb for a joining word.

example.question: Juma ___ Otieno ni marafiki.

misconceptions.cause: The child chooses a word that is already in the sentence.
misconceptions.reveals: A gap between two names, with a noun among the options.
misconceptions.help: Which word joins the two names?
misconceptions.feedback: Kiunganishi huunganisha maneno au sentensi, kama "na", "lakini" na "kwa sababu". Si nomino wala kitenzi.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Uses na for every join, even where the meaning is "but" or "because" (Nilienda na sikumpata).

example.question: Jaza: Nilienda kwake ___ sikumpata.

misconceptions.cause: Na is the first joining word learnt and covers "and" for everything.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Jaza: Nilienda kwake ___ sikumpata." with "na" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask whether the second part agrees with the first or goes against it; against means lakini.
misconceptions.feedback: Sehemu ya pili inapingana na ya kwanza, kwa hiyo tumia lakini.
misconceptions.source: English or mother-tongue interference on Kiswahili; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Swaps the reason and the result (kwa hiyo for kwa sababu).

example.question: Jaza: Hakuja shuleni ___ alikuwa mgonjwa.

misconceptions.cause: Both words link a cause and an effect; the child does not check which part is the cause.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Jaza: Hakuja shuleni ___ alikuwa mgonjwa." with "kwa hiyo" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Draw an arrow from cause to effect; kwa sababu points back to the cause, kwa hiyo forward to the result.
misconceptions.feedback: Kuwa mgonjwa ni sababu, kwa hiyo tumia kwa sababu.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

learning_experiences: kushirikiana na wenzake kueleza maana ya vihusishi na kuvitolea mifano (k.m karibu na, mbali na, juu ya, chini ya, nje ya na ndani ya),
kutambua vihusishi katika kundi la maneno aliyopewa,
kuchagua vihusishi kwenye kundi la maneno katika tarakilishi, kuviburura na kuvitia kapuni akiwa peke yake au kwenye vikundi,
kutumia vihusishi kutunga sentensi daftarini au mtandaoni kwa kuzingatia suala lengwa na masuala mtambuko mbalimbali,
kuwasomea au kuwasambazia wenzake na mwalimu sentensi alizotunga ili kuzitathmini.
key_inquiry_questions: Vihusishi vina umuhimu gani katika mawasiliano?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhiriki katika mijadala, kazi za vikundi na mawasiliano mtandaoni.
Ujuzi wa kidijitali: wanafunzi anapotumia kifaa cha kidijitali katika kutambua vihusishi na kutunga sentensi mtandaoni.
Ubunifu: mwanafunzi anapotunga sentensi akitumia vihusishi.
Kujiamini: mwanafunzi anapofaulu kutambua vihusishi na kuvitungia sentensi sahihi.
sub_strands.values:
Heshima: mwanafunzi anapothamini mchango wa wenzake katika kikundi.
Uwajibikaji: mwanafunzi anapotumia kifaa cha kidijitali katika kutambua vihusishi na kuvitungia sentensi mtandaoni.
